body.p: File conflicts happen when users modify the same file in different branches and then try to apply one branch's changes onto the other. File conflicts can occur during a merge or merge-like operation such as a rebase, cherry-pick, or revert.
To resolve a file conflict, on Git Staging, follow these steps:

ol.li:
Open the file in the compare editor to view the differences between the local and incoming version.
To do so, on Unstaged files, double-click the conflicted file. Alternatively, right-click the file to open the context menu and choose Open in compare editor.
A conflicted file's context menu

Choose how to resolve the conflict.
If both versions modify the same file and you want to keep changes from both versions:
Use the compare editor to choose which changes to keep and discard. To resolve the conflict, select Apply.
If both versions modify the same file and one version is the clear choice, use Resolve using Mine to keep the working copy version or Resolve using Theirs to accept the incoming version.
To do so, right-click a conflicted resource to open the context menu and choose Resolve conflict > Resolve using "Mine" or Resolve using "Theirs".
To mark a file conflict as resolved (even if it is not), right-click a conflicted resource and select Mark as resolved.

body.p: Resolved files are staged automatically and appear on Staged files.

During an in-progress operation, the Git Staging view identifies the current operation and lists conflicted files on Unstaged files. The Git History view shows the relationship between the merge source commit and destination commit and labels them.
